userConfirmed: The imported reference is from Tuánjié Township in Yunnan.
The visible earthen-wall surface is a representative long-term weathered state.
The visible roof-tile relationship is a representative traditional Yunnan tile reference.
The visible exterior timber colors are approved aged-timber color references.
directScanObservations: A compact inward-facing courtyard compound is visible as a whole-building scan.
Several pitched gray tiled roof masses enclose a central open void.
The outer envelope is dominated by tall earth-toned solid walls with sparse small openings.
A rough stone or masonry base and strong lower-wall weathering are visible.
The roof is visibly assembled from discrete gray pan-and-cover tile rows rather than a continuous corrugated sheet.
Exterior timber reads as low-saturation gray-brown to dark brown with exposure-dependent variation.
A stepped approach and small attached entrance-side volumes are visible at the lower side of the scan.
The compound sits in uneven or sloping terrain rather than on an abstract flat platform.
domainInformedHypotheses: The scan may contain a concealed or embedded timber frame, but its member layout is not recoverable from the current exterior view.
The visible pan-and-cover relationship is approved, while exact tile dimensions, lap, bedding, fastening, ridge and eave details remain unverified for this sample.
The dominant high volume may contain more than one usable level, but floor count and elevations are not confirmed.
